name: Fenn Roche
life: Fenn has sold boats to people who never once left the marina in them. He is very good at selling the feeling of a Saturday that doesn't yet exist. A buyer with new cushions and nowhere to put them makes the trick too literal for comfort. Thursday often includes a stop at the corner outside Coastal Barber, where Fenn usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I've been selling an imaginary fifth berth in people's daydreams. One client has already bought cushions. I owe her a phone call before she buys the boat.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a narrow-striped sweater and a watch on a cracked leather band. Fenn has heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw, with short black hair swept back. Fenn looks toward the door whenever a name is called during a conversation.
personality: Fenn talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Fenn's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To tell the buyer the truth about the nonexistent vacancy.
family: Jules Wong is Fenn’s cousin. Fenn remembers the birthdays. Jules asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *Home with stairs*, Jules says, “I priced the missing rail. My family did the original job and used the cheapest possible ending.”
connections: Sylvia Moros. A broker's imaginary vacancy has to be answered by the woman who really owns the four berths.

reactions.response: Fenn stops the lesson there and asks the rower to show the troublesome patch from a stable spot.

reactions.situation: When pressed to explain someone else's silence
reactions.response: Fenn says only what happened and lets the absent person keep their reasons.
